title: A scheme descent cocycle gives an etale equivalence relation
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\{u_i:U_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$ a jointly surjective etale covering [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Let $f_i:X_i\to U_i$ be schemes over its members. Put $U_{ij}=U_i\times_SU_j$ and $R_{ij}=X_i\times_{U_i}U_{ij}$, with projection $p_i:R_{ij}\to X_i$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Suppose given isomorphisms $\theta_{ij}:R_{ij}\xrightarrow{\sim}R_{ji}$ interchanging the two base projections. Their restrictions along $U_i\to U_{ii}$ are identities, and, after the canonical pullbacks to $U_i\times_SU_j\times_SU_k$, they satisfy $\theta_{jk}\circ\theta_{ij}=\theta_{ik}$. Form the scheme coproducts $V=\coprod_iX_i$ and $R=\coprod_{i,j}R_{ij}$ [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], with inclusions $\iota_i:X_i\to V$. Define $s,t:R\to V$ on $R_{ij}$ by $s=\iota_i\circ p_i$ and $t=\iota_j\circ p_j\circ\theta_{ij}$. Then $s,t$ are etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and $(s,t):R\to V\times_SV$ is a monomorphism identifying $R(T)$ with an equivalence relation on $V(T)$ for every $S$-scheme $T$.

source.place: Tag 02WW (spaces theorem-presentation), construction of the input etale equivalence relation from a scheme descent cocycle; the diagonal identity and triple-overlap cocycle. This is the relation-construction argument of the parent, not the quotient-existence theorem.

proof.text: The coproduct mapping property in [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] gives the structure maps $V\to S$, $R\to S$ and the stated $s,t$ from their component maps. The base-projection compatibility of $\theta_{ij}$ says that both component maps have the same composite to $S$, so $(s,t):R\to V\times_SV$ exists by [def-pc-fibre-product]. That same universal property identifies $R_{ij}$ with $X_i\times_SU_j$: a map into either scheme is a pair $(x,b)$ with $x:T\to X_i$, $b:T\to U_j$ and $u_if_ix=u_jb$. In these coordinates $p_i(x,b)=x$. Define $\tau_{ij}(x,b)=p_j\theta_{ij}(x,b)$. The two base maps of $\theta_{ij}(x,b)\in R_{ji}(T)$ are $b$ and $f_ix$, so $f_j\tau_{ij}(x,b)=b$ and its other coordinate is $f_ix$. These are morphism identities, by the uniqueness clause of the fibre-product property.

proof.text: Each $p_i:R_{ij}\to X_i$ is the base change of the etale map $u_j:U_j\to S$ along $u_if_i:X_i\to S$, using the identification in step 1. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change] makes $p_i$ etale. The analogous assertion holds for $p_j:R_{ji}\to X_j$. The inclusions $X_i\to V$ are open immersions by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]; the isomorphisms $\theta_{ij}$ are open immersions by [def-weil-open-immersion], since their image is their whole target. Apply clauses (1) and (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] to obtain etaleness of both $R_{ij}\xrightarrow{p_i}X_i\to V$ and $R_{ij}\xrightarrow{\theta_{ij}}R_{ji}\xrightarrow{p_j}X_j\to V$. Finally the $R_{ij}$ are open subschemes covering $R$, again by the coproduct statement. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-on-source] to that open cover shows that $s$ and $t$ are etale.

Restrict two arrows to R with equal endpoints along the pullback of the coproduct open cover, twice, using [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] and [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing]. On one such piece they factor through R_ij and R_kl. If i differs from k or j differs from l, disjointness of coproduct components makes the piece empty. Otherwise cancel the monic coproduct inclusions to obtain equal source projections and equal transported target projections. The first base-interchange identity gives equal other base coordinates. Apply the universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] twice to get equal arrows into R_ij. Open-cover hom-ext gives global equality. Applying this endpoint uniqueness to arrows whose composites with the displayed pullback lift agree proves the required monomorphism.

proof.text: For every i construct delta_i:X_i -> R_ii from the pair (identity_X_i,f_i) by [def-pc-fibre-product]. Its two base coordinates coincide, so the diagonal identity gives both endpoints equal to the coproduct inclusion X_i -> V. By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], the maps delta_i followed by R_ii -> R assemble to d:V -> R with s d=t d=identity_V. For any test point a:T -> V the composite d a is a reflexive arrow. This uses the same diagonal arrows as the open-partition argument but assembles them before precomposing with a.

source.place: Tag 023W (definition-descent-datum-for-family-of-morphisms), cocycle on triple overlaps; direct functor-of-points verification using schemes.tex Tags 01JB (lemma-glue), 01JC (lemma-glue-schemes), and groupoids.tex Tag 022P (definition-equivalence-relation).

proof.text: For every (i,j), construct c:R_ij -> R_ii from (p_i,p_i f_i) using [def-pc-fibre-product]. Apply the (i,j,i) cocycle to identity_R_ij, theta_ij and c. Base interchange verifies its last coordinate hypothesis. The diagonal identity for c implies p_i theta_ji theta_ij=p_i. Assemble theta_ij followed by R_ji -> R to beta:R -> R using [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. Its source is the old target and its target is the old source by the displayed identity. Composing a relation arrow with beta proves symmetry on every test scheme.

source.place: Tag 023W (definition-descent-datum-for-family-of-morphisms), cocycle on triple overlaps; direct functor-of-points verification using schemes.tex Tags 01JB (lemma-glue), 01JC (lemma-glue-schemes), and groupoids.tex Tag 022P (definition-equivalence-relation).

proof.text: For two composable relation arrows r,q on T, pull back the coproduct open cover along r and refine each member by the coproduct open cover pulled back along q, using [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] and [def-weil-open-immersion]. On each piece r factors through R_ij and q through R_kl. If j differs from k the piece is empty by disjointness, so any map to R suffices. If j=k, cancel X_j -> V in the equality of middle endpoints. By base interchange and the two fibre-product conditions, the pair (source of r,other base coordinate of q) defines c into R_il by [def-pc-fibre-product]. The (i,j,l) cocycle says that its transported endpoint equals the target of q. Thus c followed by R_il -> R has the required endpoints. Choose these local maps; on intersections they have the same endpoints, so the uniqueness proved in step 3 makes them equal. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] and its hom-ext clause to obtain the global composite arrow. Together with steps 3--5 this proves the claimed equivalence relation, also when the index type or a test scheme is empty.
